rows.selection_reason: Existing evidence is sparse, so the first experiment should test a baseline multimodal configuration to establish performance. This configuration tests PCA and ViT-L encoders with avgpool and concat, isolating key design choices. It provides a reference point for comparing aggregation/fusion strategies and encoder choices in subsequent experiments.

The existing evidence shows that config_001 (multimodal, multiprofile, pca_n2000, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, concat) achieves 0.6287 validation accuracy. This experiment tests whether switching to transformer aggregation and weighted fusion (while keeping RNA/image encoders the same) improves performance, isolating the impact of aggregation and fusion methods. This is a high-priority comparison to determine if these components are critical, without changing multiple design choices simultaneously.

Existing evidence shows that config_001 (pca_n2000 RNA, imagenet_vit_l image, avgpool, concat) achieves higher accuracy than config_007 (same encoders but transformer and weighted). This experiment tests whether changing the RNA encoder to scgpt (while keeping image encoder, aggregation, and fusion identical) impacts performance. It isolates the effect of RNA representation, a critical design choice, to determine if scgpt offers better performance than pca_n2000 in this context.

Existing evidence shows that config_001 (multimodal, multiprofile, pca_n2000 RNA, imagenet_vit_l image, avgpool, concat) achieves the highest accuracy (0.6287). This experiment tests changing the image encoder to resnet50 and fusion to weighted while keeping RNA encoder and aggregation the same. It isolates the impact of image encoder and fusion method, which are critical design choices with uncertain optimal settings. This balances exploitation (building on the top-performing config) and exploration (testing key components).

Existing evidence shows config_008 (resnet50 image encoder, weighted fusion) achieves higher accuracy than config_001 (imagenet_vit_l image encoder, concat fusion). This experiment tests whether using scgpt RNA encoder (vs pca_n2000 in config_008) affects performance when keeping image encoder, aggregation, and fusion methods constant. It isolates the RNA encoder's impact, a critical design choice with sparse evidence, while building on the promising direction of resnet50 and weighted fusion.

Existing evidence shows that config_008 (resnet50 image encoder, avgpool aggregation, weighted fusion) achieves the highest accuracy so far (0.6389). This experiment tests whether switching to transformer aggregation (while keeping resnet50 image encoder and weighted fusion) could further improve performance. It isolates the effect of aggregation method, a critical design choice, and builds on the strong foundation of config_008.

Existing evidence shows config_008 (multimodal, multiprofile, pca_n2000, resnet50, avgpool, weighted) achieves the highest accuracy (0.639). This experiment tests whether changing fusion from weighted to concat (while keeping other parameters identical) impacts performance, isolating the effect of fusion method. It is the best next step as it directly compares two critical design choices (fusion type) in a controlled manner, avoiding unnecessary parameter changes.

Existing evidence shows that config_008 (pca_n2000 RNA, resnet50 image, avgpool, weighted) achieves the highest accuracy so far. This experiment tests whether replacing the RNA encoder with scvi_n200 (while keeping image encoder, aggregation, and fusion unchanged) affects performance. This isolates the impact of RNA encoder choice, a critical design decision, and provides clarity on whether the current top-performing setup is robust to alternative encoders.

Existing evidence shows that config_006 (scvi_n200 RNA, resnet50 image, avgpool, weighted fusion) achieves the highest accuracy so far (0.6776). This experiment tests replacing avgpool with transformer aggregation while keeping RNA/image encoders and fusion method consistent. This isolates the effect of aggregation method, which is critical for understanding performance differences, and builds on the strong foundation of config_006.

Existing evidence shows that config_025 (scvi_n200 RNA, resnet50 image, transformer aggregation, weighted fusion) achieves the highest validation accuracy (0.713). This experiment tests whether changing the fusion method from weighted to concat (while keeping RNA/image encoders and aggregation the same) impacts performance. It isolates the effect of fusion strategy, a critical design choice, and builds on the strong evidence for scvi_n200/resnet50 as a promising combination.
